title: Representative short exact sequence for the coefficient layer
statement: Let X be a scheme, (A,I) an adic coefficient datum, M a derived completed-coefficient object, and n≥0. There exists a short exact sequence S of cochain complexes of sheaves over the successor finite coefficient ring such that the derived objects Q(S.X₁), Q(S.X₂), and Q(S.X₃) are respectively isomorphic to the explicit coefficient layer, the actual successor reduction, and the explicit previous object.

source.place: Tag 0942, lemma-bounded, proof (1): choose a flat-term K-flat representative and tensor the kernel-unit-quotient sequence.

proof.text: Resolve the canonical representative of M over the completed coefficient ring by a flat-term K-flat complex C. Extend scalars to the successor quotient to obtain P; change-of-rings preservation makes P K-flat with flat terms. The chosen universal derived counit, transported through the explicit quotient-to-homotopy comparison, identifies Q(P) with the successor reduction of M.

The quotient homomorphism between the finite discrete coefficient rings is surjective. Choose a set-theoretic section; its composite with any continuous coefficient-valued function is continuous because its domain is discrete. Thus the coefficient-presheaf quotient is sectionwise surjective. Sheafification preserves local surjectivity, and forgetting the module action shows the actual unit quotient map is epi. Its kernel-unit-quotient sequence is therefore short exact.

Tensor this actual coefficient sequence degreewise with P, using functoriality for its maps and differentials. Flatness of every P term preserves short exactness, and the degreewise criterion gives short exactness of complexes. The published K-flat-single tensor comparison identifies the first endpoint with the explicit layer; the tensor right unitor identifies the middle complex with P.

The ordinary scalar-last tensor swap identifies the last tensor complex with restriction of scalars of the further quotient extension of P. The actual completed projection composition equality and normalized balancing chain isomorphism identify that further extension with the previous-level extension of C. Compute the previous reduction by its K-flat counit, then use exact scalar restriction and its localization factorization to transport from the canonical representative defining the explicit previous object. Composing these isomorphisms proves the third endpoint comparison. Exactness of scalar restriction is proved directly: its composite with the faithful forgetful functor to abelian sheaves is the ordinary forgetful functor, which preserves finite limits and colimits, so reflection gives preservation for restriction.

theorem finiteQuotient_coefficient_layer_core
    (X : Scheme.{t}) {A : Type t} [CommRing A] (d : AdicCoefficientDatum A)
    (M : DerivedCategory (CompletedAdicModules X d)) (n : ℕ) :
    ∃ S : ShortComplex (CochainComplex
      (SheafOfModules.{t + 1} (completedAdicFiniteRing X d (n + 1))) ℤ),
      S.ShortExact ∧
      Nonempty (finiteQuotientLayerObject X d M n ≅ DerivedCategory.Q.obj S.X₁) ∧
      Nonempty ((completedAdicQuotientReduction X d (n + 1)).obj M ≅
        DerivedCategory.Q.obj S.X₂) ∧
      Nonempty (finiteQuotientPreviousObject X d M n ≅ DerivedCategory.Q.obj S.X₃)
